info.title: SendHeron API
info.description:
Public REST API for managing contacts, tags, sequences, enrollments, templates, emails, suppressions, sending domains and identities, analytics, and usage.

## Authentication
All endpoints require a Bearer token (API key) in the `Authorization` header.
Generate API keys from the dashboard under Settings > API Keys.

## Rate Limiting
Two one-minute ceilings apply to every request: a per-key limit, and a per-organization limit split by READ / WRITE / SEND so that reads cannot exhaust the sending budget. These limit requests; how much mail goes out in a day is under Daily sending. The multi-window throttler applies to the GraphQL dashboard API, not to this one.
Responses include `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset`; a `429` also carries `Retry-After`, and its headers name the ceiling (per-key, per-route or per-organization) that refused the request. A `429` never consumes an idempotency key. Current ceilings are readable at `GET /api/v1/usage`.

## Send outcomes
A `201` from a send route is an outcome, not proof of dispatch: `status` is `sent`; or `suppressed` with the machine-readable block reason in `errorMessage` (never retry those); or `queued` with a `holdReason`, a send that waits for capacity and goes out by itself (never retry those either). Provider failures are `503` with the FAILED attempt recorded — retry with the same idempotency key. Anything else 4xx is a request bug.

## Daily sending
Mail leaves through one shared sending account with a rolling 24-hour quota, counted per recipient (to, cc and bcc). Marketing waits once the platform reaches 80% of that quota, which keeps the rest for transactional mail; transactional waits only once the quota itself is spent.

No organization takes more than 40% of the quota: its marketing waits once everything it sent reaches that share, its transactional only once its transactional alone does. Marketing also waits above the volume the organization has proven it sends cleanly: its best day in the last 30 days times 2, and never less than 1,000 a day.

New senders warm up. Mail to an address the organization has never mailed goes out in small slices, and the next slice waits until the last one's bounces and complaints are known: 60 minutes, or 30 when people are already opening it. A slice that bounces or draws complaints past the line keeps the rest waiting until we have looked at it. Mail to people the organization already reached is never slowed by warm-up.

Contacts imported from a list whose people last heard from the sender over a year ago get the same treatment after warm-up ends: the first mail to each goes out in slices of that import (`holdReason` `IMPORT_SAMPLE`), and a slice past the line keeps the rest of that import waiting (`IMPORT_SAMPLE_FAILED`) until we have looked at it.

A send that waits is neither refused nor lost: the send route answers `201` with `status` `queued`, the reason in `holdReason` and the next attempt in `heldUntil`, and the same record (`GET /api/v1/emails/{id}`) turns `sent` when it goes. Do not retry it. Attachments are never stored, so a send carrying them cannot wait: where it would, it answers `503` with `emailSending.sendHeld`; retry with the same idempotency key later. `GET /api/v1/usage` reports the position under `sending`.

## Scopes
API keys are scoped to specific permissions. Every scope an endpoint lists is required, and they are not alternatives. Available scopes: `contacts:read`, `contacts:write`, `sequences:read`, `sequences:write`, `templates:read`, `templates:write`, `analytics:read`, `emails:send`, `suppressions:read`, `suppressions:write`, `sending:read`, `sending:write`.

name.description: Sequence name, unique within the workspace.

triggerType.description: What enrols contacts on its own once the sequence is active: manual | contact_created | list_added | tag_added | event | webhook. manual means only explicit enrollments (POST /contacts/{id}/sequences/{seqId}/enroll, the bulk route, or the dashboard). Optional on a draft: the graph's TRIGGER step carries the same information, and a graph write whose TRIGGER step is configured updates this to match, so the usual path is to leave it out here and set it in PUT /sequences/{id}/graph.

triggerConfig.description: Keys depend on triggerType, and a key the trigger does not read is refused rather than stored: tagId (UUID of a tag in this workspace) for tag_added, listId (UUID) for list_added, eventName for event, an optional source filter for contact_created. Whether the trigger is complete is checked at activation, so a draft may omit them.

ref.description: Client-local reference for this step, used by edges. Any short string, unique within the payload.

id.description: Existing step UUID to update in place. Omit to create a new step. Steps that contacts have already passed through cannot be deleted, so repairs should carry existing ids.

config.description:
Step configuration. The keys depend on `type`, and a key this step type does not read is REJECTED rather than stored: a config the worker cannot understand used to be accepted silently and simply never run.

TRIGGER: `triggerType` (manual | contact_created | list_added | tag_added | event | webhook), plus `tagId` (UUID) for tag_added, `listId` (UUID) for list_added, `eventName` for event, and an optional `source` filter for contact_created.
SEND_EMAIL: `templateId` (UUID).
DELAY: `duration` (positive number) and `unit` (minutes | hours | days). A delay of one week is {"duration": 168, "unit": "hours"} or {"duration": 7, "unit": "days"}; there is no `days` key.
CONDITION: `operator` (equals | not_equals | contains | not_contains | starts_with | ends_with | is_set | is_not_set | greater_than | less_than | has_tag | not_has_tag), `field` and `value`. `field` is a contact column (email, firstName, lastName, status) or a custom property key, compared as text; greater_than and less_than compare as numbers. is_set and is_not_set take no `value`. has_tag and not_has_tag take the tag UUID as `value` and read no `field`.
ACTION: `actionType` (add_tag | remove_tag | update_property | send_webhook), plus `tagId` or `tagName` for add_tag and remove_tag, `properties` (object) for update_property, `webhookUrl` (https) for send_webhook.

Values are validated here; whether a step is COMPLETE is checked at activation, so a draft may still omit required keys.

fromRef.description: Ref of the step this edge leaves.

toRef.description: Ref of the step this edge enters.

edgeType.description: default for linear flow; true/false only from CONDITION steps.

expectedUpdatedAt.description: Optimistic concurrency guard: the sequence's updatedAt you last read. A mismatch returns 409 instead of silently overwriting someone else's edit.

allowBranchRemoval.description: Confirm removing a true/false branch edge that a CONDITION step had before this write. Without it such a payload is refused (400 sequences.branchRemovalNeedsConfirmation): a one-branch condition is a valid graph ("stop here"), so the dropped branch would otherwise take effect silently — contacts taking that outcome just stop. Retargeting a branch (same edgeType, different destination) needs no flag.

steps.description: Every step of the sequence. The payload replaces the graph, so a step left out is deleted (refused while contacts have passed through it).

edges.description: Every edge of the sequence, by step ref.

status.description: ACTIVE resumes the sequence, and is refused unless the graph is sound: at least one step, a trigger, no orphans, and every step configured well enough to run. PAUSED stops contacts advancing while keeping their position, so resuming continues rather than restarts; while paused the sequence refuses new enrollments.

type.description: static: members are added and removed explicitly, and adding one fires the list_added sequence trigger. dynamic: a segment whose members are whoever matches `rules` when it is read; nothing is ever added to it, so list_added never fires for it.

rules.description:
Who a dynamic list contains, evaluated every time it is read. Required when `type` is dynamic, cleared when it is static.
A group is {"type": "group", "logic": and | or, "rules": [...]} whose rules are atomic rules {"type": "rule", "field": ..., "operator": ..., "value": ...} or nested groups, at most three levels deep. A bare array of atomic rules is read as an AND group.
`field` is a contact column (email | firstName | lastName | status | source | createdAt | updatedAt), `tags`, or `properties.<key>` for a custom property; any other field is refused (400 lists.invalidRuleField). `operator` is one of equals | not_equals | contains | not_contains | starts_with | ends_with | greater_than | less_than | greater_than_or_equal | less_than_or_equal | is_set | is_not_set | in | not_in. contains, not_contains, starts_with and ends_with are case-insensitive; a contact column compares as its own type and a custom property as text. is_set and is_not_set take no value; in and not_in take an array. On `tags` only in and not_in (tag names) and is_set and is_not_set (any tag at all) are accepted.

CAMPAIGN and BULK are always marketing whatever the template says, so previewing through one shows the unsubscribe block a TRANSACTIONAL template would still gain. TRANSACTIONAL_API and CAMPAIGN_TEST are always transactional. SEQUENCE and DIRECT follow the template.

Preview text: the line inboxes show after the subject, sent as a hidden preheader at the top of the body. Supports Handlebars variables. Whitespace is collapsed to one line; blank means none. At most 200 characters (templates.previewTextTooLong).
previewText.example: Your first steps, and where to find help

bodyHtml.description: HTML body, for a raw-HTML template (supports Handlebars variables). Supply exactly one of bodyHtml or document — sending both is refused rather than one silently winning.

document.description: Block document, for a builder template. The server validates it and compiles bodyHtml from it, so the compiled HTML is always exactly what the blocks say — you cannot send bodyHtml alongside it. Schema and block reference: docs/template-document.md. Validate one without saving via POST /api/v1/templates/validate.

emailType.description: Email type. Required — the type decides suppression behavior and unsubscribe handling, so it must be declared, never defaulted: a password-reset template that silently became MARKETING would be blocked for exactly the users who unsubscribed and most need it.

tagIds.description: Tag IDs to associate with this template

previewText.description: Preview text, the line inboxes show after the subject (hidden preheader). Omit to keep it; null or an empty string removes it. At most 200 characters.

document.description: Block document. An object recompiles the template from it, entering or staying in builder mode. An explicit null EJECTS to raw HTML: the document is dropped and the last compiled bodyHtml becomes editable. Omitting the field leaves the mode alone — and editing bodyHtml directly on a builder template is refused until it is ejected, so the blocks and the HTML can never disagree.

tagIds.description: Tag IDs to associate (replaces existing tags)

confirmEmailTypeChange.description: Required whenever emailType actually changes. Reclassifying a template is a compliance event — TRANSACTIONAL to MARKETING makes its sends consent-suppressible, the reverse strips unsubscribe handling — so a type change without this flag returns 400 (templates.emailTypeChangeNeedsConfirmation).

reason.description: Manual suppression reasons only. Bounce and complaint are recorded by the platform from provider events and cannot be set through this endpoint — accepting them would let a caller fabricate a deliverability record that blocks transactional mail.

note.description: Why this address is being suppressed. Shown to support.

confirmHardTier.description: Required to lift a bounce or complaint suppression. Those are deliverability facts, not preferences — re-mailing the address risks the sending domain, so it takes a deliberate acknowledgement.

note.description: Why this suppression is being lifted.

domain.description: The domain to authenticate, without scheme or path. Case and a trailing dot are normalized away. Authenticating a domain covers every address under it, including subdomains.

label.description: Human label shown when picking a sender.

fromEmail.description: The From address. Accepted when its domain is added to this workspace (verification may still be pending) or verified in another workspace of this organization, and reported as unsendable until it is authenticated here, so an identity can be prepared before the DNS is in place. Any other domain is refused.

fromName.description: Display name recipients see beside the address.

replyToEmail.description: Where replies go, when that differs from the From address. Its domain does not have to be authenticated.
